Consult Summary:
- 45-year-old woman with 3–4 months of progressive dry, cracked, sore, and intermittently itchy palmar hand skin impairing work; clinical impression: contact dermatitis; treatment plan includes avoidance (gloves), topical steroid cream, and intensive emollient therapy with follow-up in 1–2 weeks if no improvement.

History:
- Presenting complaint:
  - Soreness, cracked skin, and intermittent pruritus of the palms and fingers.
  - Patient reports skin has become painful and is interfering with ability to work.
- Timeline:
  - Symptoms began approximately 3–4 months ago after a job change.
  - Symptoms have persisted and progressed to the point of pain and functional impairment.
  - Patient has been off work for the past 3 days because of symptoms.
- Exacerbating/initiating/relieving factors:
  - Occupational exposure: works as a hotel housekeeper using bathroom cleaning products; not consistently wearing gloves. Patient suspects this is related to onset.
  - Tried over-the-counter emollient (E45) without benefit.
  - Tried an antihistamine (unspecified) without benefit.
- Associated symptoms / review of systems:
  - Intermittent itching of palms.
  - Occasional bleeding when scratching; no spontaneous bleeding reported.
  - Mild generalized dry skin (examples: legs) noted historically.
  - Denies fever, nausea, vomiting, bowel symptoms, or urinary symptoms.
  - Appetite and general wellbeing reported as maintained.
- Pertinent negatives:
  - No known prior diagnosis of eczema or dermatitis.
  - No history of asthma or inflammatory bowel disease reported.

Past Medical History:
- Type 2 diabetes mellitus.
  - Medication: Metformin — dose/route/frequency not documented.
- No other chronic medical conditions reported.
- No prior diagnosed skin conditions reported.

Allergies:
- Patient reports no known drug or other allergies.

Medications:
- Metformin — dose/route/frequency not documented.
- Tried E45 emollient (over-the-counter) — dose/route/frequency not documented.
- Tried an antihistamine — agent and dose/route/frequency not documented.

Social History:
- Occupation: Hotel housekeeper (commercial setting); cleans bedrooms and bathrooms.
  - Recently changed jobs approximately four months ago.
  - Not consistently wearing protective gloves while cleaning.
- Smoking: Denies tobacco use.
- Alcohol: Drinks a couple of pints per week.
- Substance use: No recreational drug use reported.
- Work impact: Unable to work for the past 3 days due to hand symptoms.

Family History:
- Family history of diabetes. No family skin disease reported.

Physical Examination:
- No vital signs documented.
- No physical examination findings documented in the transcript.

Investigations:
- No laboratory tests, imaging, or other investigations documented or ordered in the transcript.

Assessment & Plan:
- Issue 1: Probable contact dermatitis / irritant dermatitis of the hands (occupational exposure)
  - Assessment: Clinical impression by clinician is dermatitis, likely related to cleaning product exposure and lack of glove use.
  - Plan:
    - Avoidance of trigger exposures; strongly advised to wear protective gloves consistently while cleaning.
    - Prescribe topical steroid cream(s) for inflammation — specific agent/dose/route/frequency not documented in transcript.
    - Prescribe stronger emollients and advise liberal application (patient advised to coat on 3–4 times per day for the next couple of weeks).
    - Send prescription to patient's pharmacy (specific medication details not documented).
    - Return for review in approximately 1–2 weeks if minimal improvement; return sooner if condition worsens or spreads.
- Issue 2: Symptomatic control and topical therapy trial failure
  - Assessment: Patient reports no benefit from E45 and an antihistamine trial.
  - Plan:
    - Initiate prescribed topical steroid and more intensive emollient regimen as above.
    - Monitor response; reassess need for alternative therapies if no improvement after 1–2 weeks.
- Issue 3: Occupational impact / functional limitation
  - Assessment: Symptoms currently impair work; patient off work for 3 days.
  - Plan:
    - Advise workplace protective measures (consistent glove use).
    - Provide prescription and follow-up; consider earlier review if unable to return to work or if condition worsens.
    - No specific sick note or occupational health referral documented in transcript.

General plan items:
- Prescription to be sent to pharmacy (medication name(s) and dosing not detailed in transcript).
- Follow-up arranged: review in 10–14 days if no improvement; sooner if worsening or spreading.

Quality checks (document_quality):
- Missing but clinically expected elements:
  - No documented vital signs.
  - No skin physical examination findings (appearance, extent, presence of fissures, erythema, scaling, distribution) described.
  - No specific topical steroid name, strength, dose, route, or frequency documented.
  - No details of emollient product name or formulation beyond "stronger emollients."
  - No documentation of objective assessment of diabetes control (e.g., HbA1c, glucose readings) which may be relevant to skin healing.
  - No photography or dermatology referral documented.
  - No documented sick note, workplace accommodations, or occupational health referral details.
  - No laboratory tests or cultures ordered.
- Internal conflicts from the transcript:
  - Patient initially states no bleeding; later clarifies that scratching has caused bleeding sometimes (clarified rather than direct contradiction).
- Transcript quality:
  - Audio transcript content is clear with minimal interruptions; clinical details are adequately captured though formal physical exam and specific prescription details were not documented.
